# A Session schema for the agents sidebar

- Status: planned
- Links: [research](../../docs/research/agent-session-261020.md) · PR #18 (the agents sidebar) · PR #20 (Session in the glossary) · icebox #22 (the sign-in `session` table)

The agents sidebar keeps each row's state, task kind, title and nesting in the web app alone. `AgentState` and `AgentTask` are the keys of `stateIcons` and `taskIcons` in `web/next/src/components/agents/icons.ts`, and `title` and `subagents` sit on the row types in `agents/sidebar.tsx`. All four describe one run of an agent, which the glossary calls a Session, so they move into a `Session` schema in `packages/schema`, beside `Agent`. A subagent's run becomes a child session that points at the session that started it, as OpenCode, Codex and eve model it.

## Steps

1. Settle the open questions below with the user, one at a time.
2. Name any new term, such as the status, through the `domain-modeling` skill, and record the schema's shape in an ADR.
3. Add `packages/schema/src/session.ts` on the conventions `Agent` follows: Zod 4, keys A to Z, `Id` from `common.ts`, and a JSDoc description per field drafted from the sources' own wording. Add a Session reference page after Agent, with its sources generated by a script, as `bun run agent:schemas` generates Agent's.
4. Key `stateIcons`, and `taskIcons` if a task kind stays, by the schema's values, the way `effortIcons` is keyed by `Agent["effort"]`, and update `/docs/ui/icons`.
5. Make each sidebar row an `Agent` and its `Session`, build the nesting from the parent field, and fold `AgentRow`, `SubagentRow` and `NestedSubagentRow` into one row type.
6. Revisit icebox #22, since agent sessions then have a type of their own beside the sign-in `session` table.
7. Update the tests under `tests/web/next/src/components/agents/`, the `/docs/ui/sidebar` page and the `design` and `codebase-map` skills, and check the sidebar in a real browser.

## Decided

1. **The field's name is `status`** (2026-10-20), the name seven of the nine sources use, so the icons page's State section becomes Status.
2. **All nine values stay** (2026-10-20): cancelled, completed, failed, idle, paused, pending, running, stuck and waiting. Sessions run as CLIs in herdr panes, where a rate limit pauses a session and an unrecognized screen can leave it stuck, so each value has a way to be detected: herdr's own status (`working`, `blocked`, `idle`), the harness's wording on screen (a usage limit and its reset time), or the server (a session that stopped making progress).
3. **Stuck and waiting stay apart** (2026-10-20). Waiting: the agent asked the human something on purpose, a question or a permission, which the UI can answer. Stuck: the agent is not moving and asked nothing the server understands, such as an unrecognized screen or one that has not changed for a long time, so a person has to look at the pane.
4. **A reason and an until time beside the status** (2026-10-20): `reason`, a short text such as "rate limit" or "permission for npm test", and `until`, a time used only while paused, so the UI can count down and the server knows when to check again. Claude Code's `waitingFor`, OpenCode's retry message and next time, and Cloudflare's interrupted reason do the same.
5. **An optional task kind on the session** (2026-10-20), one of the thirteen on `/docs/ui/icons`, set by whoever starts the session (`zerosdk session start --agent builder --task debug`), since the glossary defines a subagent as started for one task, so the same agent can build one day and debug the next. No source has such a field; it is ZeroSDK's own, and a session started without one shows its status icon.
6. **A session names its agent by `Id`** (2026-10-20), as `fallbacks` already references agents, so renaming an agent never breaks its sessions; the UI shows the name by looking the `Id` up, and the server does the same when it launches Claude with `--agent`. Seven of the nine sources reference by name; OpenCode references by id.

## Open questions

Section 5 of [the research](../../docs/research/agent-session-261020.md#5-what-it-means-for-zerosdks-session) gives the evidence for each. To ask one at a time, each with a recommendation:

1. **The lineage.** Recommended: the parent alone. A depth can be counted along the chain, and a root can follow if a list ever needs one.
2. **The title, the ticket and the pull request.** Recommended: an optional title, generated and renamable, with the ticket and the pull request in fields of their own, so the row composes `ZS-12#45 Add tools` instead of storing it.
